title: A root over a residue prime avoids the localization polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f,g\in k[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $f$ monic (leading coefficient $1$), and let $L$ be a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that for a finite indexed family $(\alpha_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $L$ the coefficient image of $f$ in $L[t]$ equals $\prod_{i\in I}(t-\alpha_i)$; the empty family is allowed. Let $f_1\in k[t]$ be irreducible, meaning nonzero, not a unit, and with a unit factor in every factorization in $k[t]$. If $f_1\mid f$ and $f_1\nmid g$, then there is an index $i\in I$ such that $f_1(\alpha_i)=0$ and $g(\alpha_i)\ne0$, where evaluation [def-weil-polynomial-root] uses the given map $k\to L$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof: final residue-field paragraph, selection of i with f_1(alpha-bar_i)=0 and g-bar(alpha-bar_i) nonzero.

proof.text: Write $\iota:k\to L$ for the injective field map of [def-pc-field-extension]. The irreducible $f_1$ is nonzero and is not a unit. It is therefore nonconstant: a nonzero constant $c$ has the constant inverse $c^{-1}$. In particular it has a nonzero coefficient of positive degree. Its image in $L[t]$ is still nonconstant, since $\iota$ is injective and coefficientwise extension sends this nonzero coefficient to a nonzero coefficient. Also $f\ne0$, since its leading coefficient is $1\ne0$. These are direct coefficient statements in [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, final residue-field paragraph; expanded details of the root selection.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid], $k[t]$ is a principal ideal domain. The subset $J=\{Af_1+Bg:A,B\in k[t]\}$ is an ideal: sums and multiplication by an arbitrary polynomial preserve the displayed form. Write $J=(d)$. Since $f_1,g\in J$, $d$ divides both $f_1$ and $g$. Choose $e$ with $f_1=de$. Irreducibility says that $d$ or $e$ is a unit. If $e$ is a unit, then $d=f_1e^{-1}$, so $d\mid g$ implies $f_1\mid g$, contrary to hypothesis. Thus $d$ is a unit, $1\in J$, and there exist $A,B\in k[t]$ with $Af_1+Bg=1$. This proves the needed identity over the original base field, without assuming $f_1$ irreducible over $L$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, final residue-field paragraph; expanded details of the root selection.

proof.text: For $P\in k[t]$ write $P_L=\iota_*P\in L[t]$. The statement of [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective] gives an injective ring homomorphism $\iota_*:k[t]\to L[t]$. Choose $H\in k[t]$ with $f=f_1H$. Consequently $f_L=(f_1)_LH_L$ and $f_L\ne0$. The hypothesis already writes $f_L=\prod_{i\in I}(t-\alpha_i)$, so it splits over $L$ in the explicit finite-factorization sense of [lem-trf-divisor-of-split-polynomial]. Apply that node with $F=L$, $P=f_L$, $Q=(f_1)_L$ to obtain $d\in L$ and a finite family $(\beta_j)_{j\in J_1}$ with $(f_1)_L=d\prod_{j\in J_1}(t-\beta_j)$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, final residue-field paragraph; expanded details of the root selection.

proof.text: The nonconstant polynomial $(f_1)_L$ cannot have the empty factor list $J_1$, since an empty product gives the constant $d$. Choose $j\in J_1$ and put $\beta=\beta_j$. Evaluating its displayed factorization gives $f_1(\beta)=0$. By the evaluation ring homomorphism in [def-weil-polynomial-root] and $f=f_1H$, we have $f(\beta)=0$. Evaluating the GIVEN factorization of $f_L$ therefore gives $0=\prod_{i\in I}(\beta-\alpha_i)$. A finite product in a field is zero only if one factor is zero (induction on the number of factors, using the absence of zero divisors). Thus there is $i\in I$ with $\beta=\alpha_i$, and $f_1(\alpha_i)=0$. This argument also treats the empty $I$: its product is $1$, so under the hypotheses it would give $0=1$ and is impossible.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, final residue-field paragraph; expanded details of the root selection.

proof.text: Finally evaluate the base-field identity $Af_1+Bg=1$ of Step 2 at this $\alpha_i\in L$, using the given $k\to L$ and [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Since evaluation is a ring homomorphism and $f_1(\alpha_i)=0$, the identity becomes $B(\alpha_i)g(\alpha_i)=1$. If $g(\alpha_i)=0$, its left side is $0$, contradicting $1\ne0$ in $L$. Therefore $g(\alpha_i)\ne0$, giving both required clauses for the same index.
